resourceProfile.assessment: Canonical English, all effective Arabic runtime entries, the Arabic glossary, prior review metadata, and technical terminology searches were available.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review generation and TypeScript checking passed after all three iterations.

linguisticCritique.summary: Three complete-scope passes resolved 75 catalog, comparison, formula, unit, and engineering-terminology findings.

competentHumanReview.summary: The Arabic corrections were machine-reviewed and still require competent human review.

publicationAuthorization.summary: This cycle authorizes a locale-specific commit only, not publication or deployment.

findings.summary: Twenty-five comparison and catalog entries contained agreement errors, literal product-profile phrasing, and a corrupted 30 A current unit.
evidence: The preset-237 profile changed the protected current unit A into an Arabic letter.
Several mod profiles confused power with energy or obscured measured limits.
findings.resolution: Restored protected units and rewrote battery, material, mod, authenticity, and comparison text without changing product facts.

findings.summary: Twenty-five concept findings confused power with energy, constant current with direct current, strain with stress, and localized protected SI symbols.
evidence: SI prefix symbols k, M, m, and n had been replaced by Arabic letters.
The Joule article rendered constant current as continuous or direct current and power as energy in safety guidance.
Several visible values contained literal Unicode escape text instead of Ω.
findings.resolution: Restored technical symbols and corrected Ohm, Joule, Kirchhoff, TCR, trigonometry, heat-capacity, and SI terminology.

findings.summary: Twenty-five remaining concept entries used inconsistent heat-flux terms, altered engineering unit notation, and machine-literal wire-gauge language.
evidence: The AWG explanation translated ampacity as generic capacity and stranded construction as tabulated construction.
Several formulas expanded mm into prose while nearby formulas preserved symbols.
Heat-flux labels alternated between the defined density term and a broader heat-flow phrase.
findings.resolution: Standardized heat-flux language, preserved formula units, clarified SI conversions, and rewrote the wire-gauge explanation and practical guidance.
